## Course learning outcomes

By the end of the course you can:

1. **Explain** what makes computational research reproducible, replicable and
   open, and **audit** a published study against the five pillars and FAIR.
2. **Organize** a project so that raw data stays untouched, data is
   downloaded and checked by code, and results can be rebuilt with one command.
3. **Write** reports and notebooks in which every result is computed from
   the data when they render.
4. **Use** Git and GitHub to record, review and share work, and continuous
   integration to check it reproduces on a fresh machine.
5. **Pin and rebuild** software environments with Pixi lock files, and package
   them in containers for laptops and clusters.
6. **Automate** a multi-step analysis with a workflow manager (Snakemake; an
   introduction to Nextflow), and show that independent implementations agree.
7. **Document, license, cite and archive** a project so that others may and
   can reuse it.

## Topics by week

| Week | Topic | Lessons |
|------|-------|---------|
| 1 | Introduction to reproducibility and open science | 01, 03 (concepts); slides (PDF): [Lecture 1, Reproducibility](slides/Lecture1_Reproducibility.pdf), [Lecture 2, Open science](slides/Lecture2_Open-Science.pdf) |
| 2 | Project organization and version control: Git and GitHub | 02, 03, 04 (§1–6) |
| 3 | Portable and reproducible environments (Pixi first; Conda compared) | 04 (§7–10), 05, 05b |
| 4 | Literate programming: Jupyter and Quarto | 06, 07 |
| 5 | Containers: Docker and Apptainer | 08 |
| 6 | Workflows and automation: Snakemake and Nextflow | 09, 10 |
| 7 | Publishing, archiving and open science practice | 11, 12 |

## How the course works

Hands-on: short slides, then tutorials on one shared example, the
[LTEE project](pages/ltee-project.qmd). From Week 2 you also apply each tool
to your own research project, the capstone. Two projects are assessed:

| Project | What it is | Share of the grade | Assessed with |
|---------|------------|-------------------:|---------------|
| LTEE project | the project you build in the hands-on parts of the lessons, on GitHub, released with a Zenodo DOI | {{< meta event.grading.ltee-project >}}% | [what to hand in](assessment/ltee-project.qmd) |
| Capstone | your own existing research project (or a manageable part of it), separate from the LTEE project; public, or private and shared with the instructor; no DOI needed | {{< meta event.grading.capstone >}}% | [capstone rubric](assessment/capstone-rubric.qmd) |

The rest of the grade, the deadlines and the policies are in the official
syllabus.
